description: Combined Synopsis & Solicitation Haul-Out and Fathometer Replacement for ANT Colfax 64� ANB Solicitation Number: 52000PR270000250 (Request For Quote - RFQ) executive Summary This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services, prepared in accordance with the format in subpart 12.6 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), and as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. It is anticipated that a competitive, firm-fixed-price purchase order shall be awarded as a result of this synopsis/solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which if timely received, shall be considered by this agency. 1. Solicitation Overview Agency U.S. Coast Guard, Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) Contract Type Firm Fixed Price Purchase Order Set-Aside Information This solicitation is a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. Solicitation Number 52000PR270000250 2. Evaluation Criteria Quotes will be evaluated based on the following factors: Technical Capability: The offeror�s ability to perform the services described in the Performance Work Statement / Statement of Work (specifically, safe haul-out, blocking, and relaunch of the USCG 64-foot Aids to Navigation Boat). Past Performance: The offeror�s record of relevant and recent past performance. Price: Fair and reasonable pricing. 3. Points of Contact & Submission 3.1 Points of Contact Technical Questions (COR): Daniel Harn | Email: Daniel.P.Harn@uscg.mil Contracting Actions (Contracting Officer): Joshua Richardson | Email: Joshua.C.Richardson2@uscg.mil 3.2 Submission of Quotes Quotes must be submitted via email to Joshua.C.Richardson2@uscg.mil. The subject line of the email must include the solicitation number: 52000PR270000250. 4. Performance Work Statement (PWS) 4.1 Scope of Work The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform commercial shipyard services for the haul-out, blocking, and relaunch of the United States Coast Guard (USCG) 64-foot Aids to Navigation Boat (ANB) assigned to ANT Colfax, unless specifically noted as Government Furnished Equipment (GFE), as defined in this Statement of Work. 4.1.1 Objective The objective of this contract is to procure commercial shipyard services for the haul-out, blocking, and relaunch of the United States Coast Guard (USCG) 64-foot Aids to Navigation Boat (ANB) assigned to ANT Colfax. While the vessel is out of the water, ESD NOLA shall replace the existing fathometer system (including hull transducer and display/processing units as applicable). 4.1.2 Background The ANT Colfax 64� ANB requires an operational fathometer for safe navigation during its Aids to Navigation mission. The current system is inoperable, requiring a complete replacement that necessitates drydocking or hoisting the vessel out of the water to access the hull penetrations. 4.2 Specific Tasks and Requirements The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and facilities necessary to perform the following tasks, unless specifically noted as Government Furnished Equipment (GFE): Task 2.1: Haul-Out & Blocking: The Contractor shall haul out the 64� ANB using a travel lift, marine railway, or drydock capable of safely handling the vessel�s weight and dimensions. The vessel shall be safely blocked and supported in accordance with standard marine practices and USCG specifications to allow safe access to the hull. Task 2.2: Hull Cleaning (Optional/As Needed): N/A Task 2.3: Existing Equipment Removal: ANT Colfax personnel will assist ESD NOLA with removal of old fathometer once boat is hauled. (Contractor�s responsibility is limited to providing safe shipyard access and support). Task 2.4: Hull Preparation: N/A Task 2.5: New Fathometer Installation: ANT Colfax personnel will assist ESD NOLA with replacement of new fathometer. Task 2.6: Electrical Integration: ESD NOLA will assist or fix any electrical work needed. Task 2.7: Relaunch: Upon completion of the installation and initial visual inspection, the Contractor shall lift and relaunch the vessel into the water. The Contractor shall leave the vessel in the slings/blocks in the water for a sufficient time to inspect the new hull penetration for any leaks before final release. 4.2.8 Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Fathometer System: The USCG ESD NOLA has the new fathometer system. Vessel Delivery: USCG personnel will deliver the 64� ANB to the Contractor�s facility and operate the vessel during sea trials. 4.2.9 Quality Assurance and Testing Watertight Integrity Test: Prior to final acceptance, ANT Colfax and ESD NOLA will visually inspect the transducer hull penetration while the vessel is in the water to verify there is zero water ingress. Operational Testing: Following relaunch, USCG personnel will conduct an operational test (Sea Trial) of the new fathometer system to ensure it powers on, reads depth accurately, and integrates properly without electrical interference. 4.3 Deliverables Deliverable Description Due Date Report/Service Completion Completion of safe haul-out, drydock/blocking support and access, and leak-free relaunch upon completion of services, verified by the Watertight Integrity Test and Operational Testing. Within 3 days of the vessel�s arrival at the Contractor�s facility. 4.4 Place of Performance The Contractor�s designated shipyard/facility. The facility must be located within a navigable and reasonable distance of transit from ANT Colfax. 4.5 Period of Performance The haul-out, installation, and relaunch shall be completed within 3 days of the vessel�s arrival at the Contractor�s facility. Proposed Start Date: 01FEB2027. Work shall be performed Monday through Friday during normal operating hours, unless otherwise coordinated with the Point of Contact. 5. Invoicing It is a mandatory requirement that all invoicing for Purchase Orders be entered and processed through the Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) at www.ipp.gov. 6. title: Switzerland – Electrical installation work – PWA-B2, B3 (Selektiv) Ausschreibung Elektro, BKP 232 Niederspannungsinstallationen
description: Die Infrastruktur des Flughafens Zürich unterliegt einem schrittweisen Erneuerungsprozess. In den letzten 15 Jahren sind verschiedene Teile der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur umfassend saniert und erweitert worden: Das Dock B wurde komplett umgebaut, der Terminal 2 totalsaniert und erweitert, und zwischen den Terminal 1 und 2 wurde das neue Sicherheitskontrollgebäude mit zentralisiertem Zugang in das Airside Center erstellt. Derzeit werden die zentrale Gepäcksortieranlage nördlich des Terminal 1 erweitert und das flughafenweite Gepäcksortiersystem abgelöst und erneuert. In einem nächsten Schritt müssen die in die Jahre gekommenen Teile der zentralen Flughafen- Infrastruktur ersetzt werden: Das Dock A wurde zusammen mit dem Tower 1985 in Betrieb genommen und blieb in seiner Struktur bis heute weitgehend unverändert. Bezüglich Funktionalität, Nachhaltigkeit und Qualität kann das Dock A die heutigen Anforderungen nicht mehr erfüllen. Aufgrund einer umfassenden Analyse wurde entschieden, das bestehende Dock A durch einen Neubau nördlich des heutigen Gebäudes zu ersetzen. Der Ersatzneubau für das Dock A, der neue Tower und das umfassend sanierte Vorfeld zum Dock A mit allen weiteren Anpassungen, Erweiterungen und Umbauten der zentralen Flughafeninfrastruktur sind die sichtbar wichtigsten baulichen Massnahmen der nächsten 15 bis 20 Jahre. Bei der etappenweisen Realisierung muss gewährleistet werden, dass der Betrieb normal weitergeführt werden kann und mit den neu erstellten Gebäuden die künftigen funktionalen Anforderungen erfüllt werden können. Das Projekt PWA «Perimeterfreilegung Wurzel A» beinhaltet die Umsetzung von Anpassungen an bestehenden Medien und Anlagen. Diese befinden sich im und auch ausserhalb des Abbruchsperimeters der Wurzel Dock A. Die Arbeiten sind für den Bauzustand des Rückbaus und für die weiteren Phasen des Ersatzneubau Dock A im Zeitraum von 2026-2033 zu realisieren. Im Abbruchperimeter der Dockwurzel A sind essenzielle Teile der Gebäudetechnik für die Versorgung des Kontroll-Towers, Dockwurzel A, Dock A, Airside Center und der Passkontrollhalle verortet.

title: France – Software package and information systems – Evaluation des tiers 2027
description: Acquisition d’une solution d’évaluation des tiers en mode SaaS pour le compte de la Direction Juridique et Compliance. En France, la loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 relative à la transparence, à la lutte contre la corruption et à la modernisation de la vie économique (ci-après « Loi SAPIN II ») impose la mise en place d’un dispositif de prévention et de lutte contre la corruption et le trafic d’influence. Parmi les mesures à mettre en place, les entreprises doivent procéder à l’évaluation de leurs tiers (clients, fournisseurs, partenaires, intermédiaires…) préalablement à l’entrée en relation d’affaires. Plusieurs législations étrangères ayant un champ d’application extraterritorial imposent aux entreprises des obligations analogues. En outre, la loi française n°2017-399 du 27 mars 2017 relative au devoir de vigilance des sociétés mères et entreprises donneuses d'ordre, loi codifiée aux articles L 225-102-4 et L 225-102-5 du code de commerce (ci-après "loi Devoir de vigilance") impose aux sociétés mères de s'assurer que toutes leurs filiales, sous-traitants et fournisseurs, respectent "les droits humains et les libertés fondamentales, la santé, et la sécurité des personnes ainsi que l'environnement". Le Groupe SNCF doit également se conformer aux législations et réglementations françaises, européennes ou étrangères applicables en matière de sanctions économiques et de contrôle des exportations, ainsi qu’à celles relatives à la lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux et le financement du terrorisme. Les entités du Groupe SNCF souhaitent se doter d’un système d’informations permettant une évaluation exhaustive de leurs portefeuilles de tiers, avec une profondeur d’analyse variable en fonction de plusieurs critères tels que la catégorie de tiers et le profil de risques du tiers, afin d’être en conformité avec les exigences règlementaires exposées ci-dessus. Le présent document constitue un cahier des charges d’expression de besoin. Il a pour objectif de décrire les grandes fonctionnalités attendues du système d’informations dédié à l’évaluation des tiers. L’objectif est de disposer d’une solution permettant l’automatisation de l’évaluation de 90 % du portefeuille total des tiers afin de minimiser l’emploi des ressources internes des entités SNCF, permettre aux opérationnels (niveau 1) de concentrer leurs efforts sur l’évaluation de 10 % restant des tiers et permettre aux responsables conformité (niveau 2) de concentrer leurs efforts sur l’évaluation des tiers à risque moyen ou fort, soit environ 5 % maximum du portefeuille total de tiers à évaluer. La consultation a pour objet de sélectionner un prestataire qui sera chargé de : • Fournir la solution logicielle, • Adapter en tant que de besoin cette solution aux besoins propres à SNCF • Assurer l’assistance et le maintien en conditions opérationnelles de la solution, • Assister au pilotage de la mise en place de la solution dans le contexte SNCF, • Produire les documents techniques et fonctionnels nécessaires à la mise en place de la solution, • Apporter un appui à la formation et au déploiement de la solution au sein de SNCF. La solution doit permettre à l’entité utilisatrice de disposer d’une évaluation complète des tierces parties (personnes morales et personnes physiques : clients, fournisseurs, intermédiaires, sous-traitants, partenaires...) avant d’engager une relation d’affaires ou dans le cadre du suivi d’une relation d’affaires en cours d’exécution. L’évaluation du tiers doit permettre d’identifier et d’apprécier le risque spécifique induit par la relation d’affaires envisagée ou en cours dans les domaines suivants : • La probité, corruption : la solution permet de se conformer aux dispositions de la loi Sapin II, UKBA (UK), FCPA (USA). Elle devra être compatible avec les recommandations de l’Agence Française Anticorruption (l’AFA.) en matière d’évaluation des tiers, • La lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux et le financement du terrorisme : il convient d’évaluer la probité du tiers au regard de sa possible condamnation ou mise en cause pour des infractions de blanchiment d’argent ou de financement du terrorisme, • Les sanctions économiques internationales et le contrôle des exportations (listes de sanctions internationales financières ou économiques, notamment celles émises par la France, l’Union européenne, les Etats-Unis et le Royaume-Uni visant notamment les personnes morales, dirigeants, administrateurs, et bénéficiaires effectifs. La solution doit permettre de remonter en standard les chaînes actionnariales des sociétés et d’identifier l’ensemble des personnes physiques sanctionnées (bénéficiaires effectifs, dirigeants, administrateurs). • La RSE (responsabilité sociétale de l’entreprise) et le devoir de vigilance : la solution devra permettre une évaluation des tiers sur les risques d’atteintes graves envers l’environnement, des droits humains et libertés fondamentales, santé et sécurité, conformément notamment à la loi sur le devoir de vigilance des entreprises donneuses d’ordre du 25 mars 2017.

description: Subject: Revenue Cycle Modernization & Innovation (RCMI) & Charge Description Master (CDM) Support Services to Defense Health Agency (DHA) Resources & Personnel Integration (R&PI), J-8 Financial Operations. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses to the RFI will not be returned. At this time, questions concerning the composition and requirements for a future RFP will not be entertained. 2.0 SUBJECT: The DHA R&PI, J8 Financial Operations is obtaining information for a potential non-personal services contract to provide administrative and technical execution services, as well as technical expertise, for the Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) activities, to include CDM optimization, enhancement, and operations, to support the DHA Electronic Health Record (EHR), Military Health System (MHS) GENESIS, and its itemized billing solution, RevX. 3.0 BACKGROUND: The DHA J-8 recognizes the need to enhance its RCM processes to ensure the efficient and effective management of healthcare finances within the MHS. Using the MHS GENESIS EHR as a catalyst, J-8 seeks to address several critical challenges within its RCM framework: Revenue Leakage and Inefficiencies, Compliance and Regulatory Risks, Data Accuracy and Integration, Patient Experience, Resource Utilization, Financial Transparency, Clean Audit Capability, and Technology and Innovation. In response to these challenges, DHA J-8 aims to launch the RCM Initiative to transform its RCM processes. The goal is to enhance workload capture, financial performance, compliance, patient satisfaction, and resource utilization while ensuring transparency and embracing innovative technologies within the MHS. Industry practice is to document, and bill patient encounters based on an itemized list of charges. To ensure documented care in MHS GENESIS results in an all-inclusive itemized bill within RevX, numerous actions must occur throughout the revenue cycle process (assignment of Patient Identification Process (PIP), provider documentation, medical record coding, and patient billing). Administration staff must ensure the PIP providers completely document and select the proper patient orderable description of care provided. Medical record coders must properly code the care provided. Finally, Uniform Business Office (UBO) staff must properly generate a bill on established separate billing forms for professional charges and institutional charges. The DHA supports and provides medical care for the Department of War, 9.4 million eligible beneficiaries through the $52 billion Defense Health Program (DHP), which includes contracted healthcare networks and Military Treatment Facilities (MTFs). The deployment of MHS GENESIS is complete and currently in a transition phase. While this major technology transformation has provided a significant set of enhanced revenue cycle and business management capabilities for the MHS, they have also brought new requirements to align with industry-leading practices and underscored underlying issues in the legacy environment. For the Government to fully realize the benefits of MHS GENESIS revenue cycle capabilities, these cross-functional challenges require an integrated approach to resolve. The Government will direct the actual implementation and detailed tasks for the RCM Activity as the MHS lacks knowledgeable in-house staffing to execute these specific operations. title: License to Access the American Hospital Association Inc.�s (AHA) Proprietary Databases, Training, and Technical Support
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention intends to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order to American Hospital Association (AHA) for the Office of Public Health data, Surveillance, and Technology, OPHDST/IDD/ADB, to maintain and continue licenses to access AHA�s proprietary Annual Survey, AHA Healthcare IT, Payment, and Financial databases, and associated software, online tools, virtual training, and technical /consultative support. The American Hospital Association, Inc. (AHA) conducts multiple surveys with hospitals to include the Annual Survey, which is the main survey that profiles a universe of 6,200+ hospitals and 400 health care systems throughout the United States. Comprising over 1,300+ hospital data points gathered directly from the source, the AHA Annual Survey Database (ASDB) offers facility-level insights on different topics including organizational structure and affiliations; beds and utilization; staffing with physicians included; expenses; accreditations and approval codes; and telehealth and remote patient monitoring. AHA also provides a Healthcare IT Database which provides information on several healthcare IT indicators that illustrate the depth and level of technology integration within hospitals. The database contains hospital level information on over 2,600 hospitals. This IT survey is the most reliable source of hospital IT implementation information available and is used as a foundation for national research and government studies, including national EHR adoption rates. In addition to these surveys, AHA also provides financial module data, a third-party database developed by AHA largely as a service/support element for clients of the AHA ASDB. AHA�s survey data is the only available data source solely focused on hospital and health system characteristics. This contract action is for services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b) (SAP). title: 6640--Vitek MS prime
description: DESCRIPTION The Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6, intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Biomerieux INC. for the purchase of bioMérieux VITEK MS Prime MALDI-TOF reagents and consumables and ChromID MRSA agar, at the Durham VA Medical Center (VAMC). Justification for this sole source procurement is in accordance with FAR 12.102(A) soliciting from a single source. MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry (MS), a TOF analyzer measures the mass-to-charge (m/z) ratio of the charged molecules. It is essential to identify and differentiate microbes when conducting tests to diagnose diseases and select appropriate antimicrobial treatment. One of the most potent proteomics methods, MALDI-TOF MS, is a rapid, precise, and economical way to recognize and differentiate microbes, such as bacteria, viruses, parasites, and fungi. This technology produces specific mass spectra fingerprints unique to each microorganism and thus can identify them accurately at the genus and species level. It reduces the time to identification from 24-48 hours to less than 30 minutes. The VITEK MS PRIME database enables the identification of 1,585 species, including 16,000 unique strains of bacteria, yeasts, and molds within minutes. With an average of 12 strains per species and enhanced workflow efficiency, the VITEK MS PRIME ensures accurate and robust species identification. However, any business that believes it can meet these requirements and possesses relevant past experience, and expertise may give written notice. title: Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing
description: The Department of the Navy Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager (DRPM) / Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Robotics and Autonomous Systems (RAS) hereby issues this announcement regarding a forthcoming Area of Interest (AOI) for Medium Unmanned Surface Vehicles (MUSV) Phase II Integration and Testing. MUSV uses modular design principles to create adaptable and resilient solutions that can effectively counter evolving threats. We invite interested parties with expertise in innovative solutions to complex problems, vessel construction, autonomy, perception systems, and general maritime experience to participate in this opportunity. Vendors will be evaluated on platform maturity, open-architecture autonomy compatibility, endurance, payload integration capacity, and rapid-production scalability. To meet the critical operational demand signal for high-volume autonomous vessel procurement over the next decade, DRPM RAS will employ innovative and streamlined acquisition pathways. The government will leverage the authorities of 10 U.S.C. 3458 (Commercial Solutions) and 10 U.S.C. 4022 (Other Transactions) and intends to award Basic Ordering Agreements and prototype other transaction agreements, and potentially production contracts or transactions to successful vendors. To maintain technical superiority and capture rapid commercial innovations, DRPM RAS intends to issue the AOI with a rolling open window. This open call will allow new entrants to compete and existing vendors to submit updated product blocks and modular payload configurations. Approved platforms will be accepted into the maritime marketplace hosted on drones.mil. This digital clearinghouse will empower authorized acquisition authorities and operational stakeholders across the Department of War enterprise to rapidly configure and issue funded delivery orders for vetted maritime autonomous systems without redundant procurement cycles. Formal AOI release is planned on or before September 30, 2026. Detailed AOI instructions will be released via SAM.gov and syndicated at https://drones.mil. Interested industry vendors capable of delivering commercial or dual-use maritime unmanned surface systems are encouraged to ensure active SAM.gov registrations and monitor this notice for amendments, industry day announcements, and formal AOI documentation. All inquiries concerning this notice must be submitted in writing to the Agreements Officer at Christopher.j.murr.civ@us.navy.mil (note this email is distinct/different than the auto generated SAM.gov). ______________________________________________________________________________________________________________Update_as_of_23_September_2026_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ DRPM RAS is issuing this Call For Solutions (CFS) under the Drone Marketplace Commercial Solutions Opening W58RGZ26SC001. The presolicitation notice N0003926RR002 (notice ID N0003926R0R02) has resulted in the CFS W58RGZ-26-S-C001-0008 issued herein. The CFS posting is in place of the aforementioned Area of Interest (AOI), a separate AOI will not be posted. All parties are encouraged to review the specific terms of the CFS posted as an attachment to this SAM.gov posting.

title: Switzerland – Lamps and light fittings – UNI - Bastions Central _ CFC233.00 - Lustrerie sur mesure
description: L’Université Bastion à Genève fait l’objet d’un projet global de rénovation visant une transformation à la fois architecturale et fonctionnelle de l’ensemble existant. L’objectif des travaux est une revalorisation durable de la structure bâtie, en tenant compte des exigences actuelles en matière d’architecture, d’usage, de technique et d’efficacité énergétique. L’accent est mis sur le développement respectueux du patrimoine bâti historique, tout en intégrant des standards contemporains sur le plan des infrastructures et de l’expression architecturale. Dans ce contexte, des aspects tels que la qualité des espaces, la flexibilité des usages ainsi qu’une approche architecturale claire jouent un rôle central. Les travaux ont d’ores et déjà débuté et l’exploitation du site se poursuit actuellement dans un contexte de chantier en cours. La mise en service est prévue pour l’année académique 2027 / 2028. Cet appel d'offre se déroulera en deux phases. Au premier tour, les soumissionnaires devront fournir les documents demandés ainsi que les échantillons de la lentille et du support en métal, selon les indications de l'appel d'offres. title: Herring Biological Sampling
description: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) requires laboratory services to process biological samples collected from British Columbia (BC) commercial herring fisheries, test fisheries, and research activities. The biological information obtained through sample processing supports annual stock assessments and the development of scientific advice regarding the status of BC herring stocks. The Contractor will be required to provide all qualified personnel, laboratory facilities, equipment, materials, and services necessary to process approximately 200 to 250 herring samples per year. Each sample typically contains approximately 100 fish, although sample sizes may vary. The Contractor must process all samples provided by DFO, including samples containing fewer than 100 fish, in accordance with DFO-approved scientific procedures. For each fish processed, the Contractor must record the fish's length, weight, sex, gonad length, gonad weight, maturity stage, and one suitable herring scale for subsequent age determination. All sample identification information and biological data must be entered into the MS Access database provided by DFO. The Contractor must also prepare herring scale slides, maintain daily electronic data backups, conduct quality control checks, and submit the required data and associated materials within the specified timelines. The Contractor must provide a minimum two-person team consisting of one Project Manager and one Sampling Technician. The team must be available to process a minimum of five herring samples per day, with each sample containing approximately 100 fish. The Contractor must provide an appropriate laboratory facility with suitable workspace, equipment, cold-storage capacity, water supply, sanitation, and arrangements for the proper disposal of biological waste. Where the facility is located more than 10 km from the Pacific Biological Station (PBS), the Contractor will be responsible for arranging and paying for the pickup and transportation of samples from PBS to the facility. Processing activities are anticipated to take place annually between March 1 and May 15, with all processing completed by May 15 unless otherwise authorized by the DFO Project Authority. The Contractor must coordinate sample receipt or pickup with DFO, provide weekly submissions of prepared herring scale slides and original sample labels during the processing period, and return cleaned, empty sample buckets strapped in groups of ten. Daily electronic data backups must be completed using the USB drive provided by DFO. The Contractor must provide a completed MS Access database containing all required biological and sample information, prepared herring scale slides suitable for subsequent age determination, original sample labels, electronic data backup files, and cleaned sample buckets. All work must be performed in accordance with DFO's Procedures for Collecting and Processing British Columbia Herring Samples and any additional instructions provided by the DFO Project Authority. The initial Contract period and each option year are expected to require similar services and sample-processing volumes. The actual number of samples provided may vary according to sample availability. Payment will be made only for samples provided by DFO and services completed in accordance with the Statement of Work. The Contractor is responsible for all costs associated with performing the work, including personnel, facilities, equipment, materials, transportation where required, and waste disposal. All proposed personnel must be fluent in English and capable of understanding technical instructions, following scientific procedures, and communicating effectively with DFO personnel.

title: Belgium – Construction work – Bouwen van FacThory 2/3 te Genk
description: Deze opdracht betreft de realisatie van een bedrijfsverzamelgebouw voor de innovatieve maakeconomie FacThory 2/3 te Genk in opdracht van Mo-Thor NV. De opdracht wordt onderverdeeld in volgende vijf delen: Deel 1, ruwbouw, afwerking en algemene coördinatie der werken Dit deel omvat alle voorbereiding van het bouwterrein, grondwerken, structuurwerken, metselwerken, rioleringswerken, dakwerken en buitenschrijnwerk. Alle afwerkingen zoals pleisterwerken, lichte wanden, systeemwanden, vloerafwerkingen en plafonds, binnenschrijnwerk, vaste uitrustingen en schilderwerken, … (niet limitatief), maken eveneens deel uit van dit deel. De coördinatieopdracht, zijnde alle taken en verantwoordelijkheden die betrekking hebben op de coördinatie in tijd en ruimte tussen de verschillende delen van de Opdracht, behoort eveneens tot het takenpakket van de Aannemer. Deel 2, elektriciteit, data en veiligheidsinstallaties Dit deel omvat alle elektrische -, data- en veiligheidsinstallaties binnen en buiten het gebouw. De aannemer aan wie dit deel van de werken wordt toegewezen, en die als onderaannemer van de algemene hoofdaannemer zal optreden, zal als Aangeduide Onderaannemer worden vermeld in de Aanvraag tot Deelneming, voor zover deze voor de Kandidaat noodzakelijk is om aan de kwalitatieve selectievoorwaarden te voldoen. Deel 3, HVAC, sanitair en brandbestrijdingsinstallaties Dit deel omvat alle verwarmings-, ventilatie- en luchtbehandelingsinstallaties met inbegrip van alle elektrische voorzieningen hiertoe, alsook het gebouwbeheersysteem. Daarnaast omvat dit deel alle sanitaire- en brandbeveiligingsinstallaties binnen en buiten het gebouw met inbegrip van de pompinstallaties en alle elektrische voorzieningen hiertoe. Ook de sprinklerinstallatie maakt deel uit van dit deel. De aannemer aan wie dit deel van de werken wordt toegewezen, en die als onderaannemer van de algemene hoofdaannemer zal optreden, zal als Aangeduide Onderaannemer worden vermeld in de Aanvraag tot Deelneming, voor zover deze voor de Kandidaat noodzakelijk is om aan de kwalitatieve selectievoorwaarden te voldoen. Ter info wordt hierbij meegedeeld dat er zal aangesloten worden op een bestaande KWO-installatie. Deel 4, liften Dit deel omvat de liftinstallaties binnen het project. De aannemer aan wie dit deel van de werken wordt toegewezen, en die als onderaannemer van de algemene hoofdaannemer zal optreden, zal als Aangeduide Onderaannemer worden vermeld in de Aanvraag tot Deelneming, voor zover deze voor de Kandidaat noodzakelijk is om aan de kwalitatieve selectievoorwaarden te voldoen. Deel 5, omgevingsaanleg Dit deel omvat onder meer de grondwerken ten behoeve van de terreinaanleg, terreinverhardingen en bijhorende rioleringswerken, groenaanleg en buitensignalisatie (niet limitatief). De aannemer aan wie dit deel van de werken wordt toegewezen, en die als onderaannemer van de algemene hoofdaannemer zal optreden, zal als Aangeduide Onderaannemer worden vermeld in de Aanvraag tot Deelneming, voor zover deze voor de Kandidaat noodzakelijk is om aan de kwalitatieve selectievoorwaarden te voldoen. De te realiseren gebouwen en infrastructuur, de visie, gehanteerde uitgangspunten en beoogde doelstellingen, het voorziene materiaalgebruik en uitvoeringswijze, worden bondig toegelicht inde Projectdefinitie, dewelke als Bijlage 6 bij deze Selectieleidraad is gevoegd. Daarnaast wordt het aanvraagdossier voor stedenbouwkundige vergunning (enkel de plannen) als Bijlage 7 bij deze Selectieleidraad gevoegd, zodat de Kandidaten zich een beeld kunnen vormen van de beoogde realisatie, doch louter ter informatie en zonder dat de Kandidaten hieraan enige rechten kunnen ontlenen.

title: NWS Earle Annual Tank Inspections and Services
description: N4008527Q0002-Annual Tank Inspections at Naval Weapons Station Earle, Colts Neck, New Jersey This notice is being issued strictly for Market Research, information and planning and purposes only and shall not be construed as either a solicitation or obligation or commitment on the part of the Government. There will not be a solicitation, specifications, or drawings available at this time. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to help The Department of the Navy, Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC), Naval Weapons Station Earle (NWSE), understand industry best practices and sources capable of meeting the requirements detailed by this announcement. NWSE welcomes responses from all interested parties; however, no decision or award of contract will be made based on responses from industry. NWSE will not pay for the preparation of, nor the subsequent use of information submitted in response to this Sources Sought. Respondents will not be notified of the outcome of NWSE�s review of the information received. Additionally, NWSE does not intend to hold discussions concerning this Sources Sought with any interested parties, but reserves the right to contact contractors if additional information is required for clarifications as it pertains to this request for information (RFI). Requirement: NWSE intends to contract for Annual Tank Inspection and Repair Service Calls for approximately 40 above ground fuel tanks, 9 drum storage areas, 4 mobile truck tanks, 1 underground UST tank located at various locations throughout NWSE. The Contractor shall provide all materials and services to test, calibrate, adjust and cathodic protection, automatic tank gauging and fuel management systems on above-ground tank, underground tanks (to include piping) piers and quay walls and associated equipment. To that end, NWSE seeks to gather information about sources able to meet this requirement. The NAICS Code for this requirement is 811310 - Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance. The associated small business size standard for this industry is $12,500,000.00. Instructions to Contractors: All interested contractors are encouraged to submit a response clearly demonstrating their capability to perform this requirement. Proposals are not being requested at this time. Responses to this Sources Sought cannot be considered as offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a contract. No formal solicitation exists at this time and no set-aside decision has been made. Responses to this Sources Sought should include the following information: 1. Title of the requirement; Company Name; Address; and Point of Contact (POC) name, phone number, and email address. 2. Company profile to include office location(s), DUNS number/CAGE Code, NAICS, and a statement regarding current small business status to include small business type(s)/certification(s) such as: 8a, WOSB, EDWOSB, HUBZone, SDVOSB, etc. 3. Specific experience (private and/or government) in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and/or Connecticut performing tank inspection, and repair building, utility, and general tank inspection services under the United Facilities General Specifications (UFGS). Statements should describe the dollar value, indicate whether your firm acted as the prime or subcontractor, list a customer Point of Contact with phone number, and provide description of the experience and how the referenced experience relates to the services described herein. A maximum of five (5) project examples reflecting the firm's experience should be submitted. Please submit responses by 16 November 11:00AM EST directly to James Martin, Contracting Officer, via email at james.j.martin3.civ@us.navy.mil. Please reference the solicitation number and title in the subject of your message. Please limit your responses to standard documents (i.e. Microsoft Office, Adobe PDF, etc.). Do not send compressed (I.e. .zip or .exe extension) or other file types, as they will be stripped from your message.

Vendors must satisfy applicable small business eligibility requirements, including any applicable nonmanufacturer rule. Quotations shall be emailed to r3phillips@bop.gov. The Government may make award without discussions. The Government will verify registration, exclusions, responsibility, and small-business eligibility before award. Issuance of this RFQ does not obligate the Government to make an award or reimburse quotation preparation costs. Payment will be made by electronic funds transfer in accordance with FAR 52.232-33, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer�System for Award Management. title: CGC STURGEON BAY ANNUAL WATER MIST INSPECTION
description: The United States Coast Guard Deputy Commandant for Systems (DCS) is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation on behalf of the Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC) to award a firm-fixed-price service contract, as detailed in the attached Statement of Work. This requirement consists of performing all on-site labor and services to conduct the annual inspection and testing of the Hi-Fog Water Mist Fire Suppression System in support of the CGC STURGEON BAY. All work must be performed on-site at CGC STURGEON BAY, 85 Port Terminal BLVD, Bayonne, NJ 07002. The planned Period of Performance (PoP) is from 11JAN27 through 15JAN27. This acquisition is a 100% total small business set-aside under NAICS code 336611. The applicable Product Service Code is j998. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforming to the solicitation is most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: 1. Technical Capability (Pass/Fail) 2. Past Performance (Pass/Fail) 3. Total Price A quotation must receive an Acceptable rating for all non-price factors to be eligible for award. Among all acceptable quotations, award will be made to the responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price. To establish Technical Capability (Pass/Fail), the quotation must demonstrate a clear understanding of the work statement requirements, conform strictly to all specifications in the attached Statement of Work, and provide any adequate capability and corporate experience documentation required by the solicitation. Failure to meet these criteria will render the quotation unacceptable. The Government will evaluate recent (completed within the last three years) and relevant past performance to assess the likelihood of successful performance. Past performance will be evaluated on an acceptable or unacceptable basis. To receive an acceptable rating, past performance must demonstrate a rating of satisfactory or higher performance of similar work. Offerors without recent or relevant past performance will be assessed as "Neutral" and considered acceptable for award. Past performance demonstrating marginal or below performance is unacceptable. Offerors shall identify all subcontractors anticipated to perform work under this contract. For each subcontractor, the offeror shall provide the subcontractor�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, the specific work items/specifications they will perform, and the percentage of work they will execute. Submit offers electronically via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government does not prescribe a specific quotation format. Offerors must submit a quotation that clearly identifies the items offered and demonstrates compliance with the stated requirements. Submissions must be complete, clear, and presented in a format that allows effective evaluation by the Government. Submit all questions via email to the points of contact identified in this notice. The Government will not accept telephone inquiries. Submit offers on a firm-fixed-price basis. Prices must be all-inclusive and must cover all costs associated with providing the services, including but not limited to manufacturing, packaging, handling, transportation, duties, tariffs, fees, and any other costs. The Government may consider offers nonresponsive if they include conditional pricing, price escalation language, or statements indicating that prices are subject to adjustment based on future costs or fees. The Government intends to evaluate offers and make award without discussions; therefore, offerors should submit their best offer with initial submission. The Statement of Work and the list of applicable FAR provisions and clauses are attached to this notice.

title: Digital Repository Platform and Physical Library Management System
description: The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration is seeking information from interested parties and potential vendors and systems integrators to implement a web-based Digital Repository (Virtual Library) Platform integrated with specialized Physical Library Management functionality. The primary purpose of this platform is to serve as a centralized hub providing standardized access to industry consensus standards, regulatory documentation, and reference literature applicable to LNG facility safety. The platform should allow access through IP verification or username/password, support concurrent users, and not require any additional software to be installed on the user�s computer or server. The solution must seamlessly handle distinct tier-based access controls across geographically dispersed stakeholder groups, support concurrent platform usage, enforce digital rights management (DRM), track visitor engagement, and provide administrative reporting for PHMSA management. Responding to this RFI is strictly voluntary. description: Notice of VISN-Based Solicitation Structure Since release of the prior draft solicitation, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has refined the acquisition strategy for Real Estate Acquisition Support Services to align with the Veterans Health Administration�s (VHA) evolving regional operating model. This revised approach supports VA�s broader Restructure for Impact and Sustainability Effort (RISE), an organizational transformation directed by Executive Order 14210. title: TSA PreCheck Travel Industry Partnership Request for Information
description: 1. DESCRIPTION Background: The TSA TTC Office is requesting information and conducting market research to understand the level of interest from industry, particularly travel industry partners such as airlines and other travel-related companies, in partnering with TSA to increase TSA PreCheck enrollments. Objectives: TSA�s primary objective is to expand TSA PreCheck participation by increasing the total number of program members, also known as Known Traveler Number (KTN) holders. The TSA PreCheck program provides significant benefits to both TSA and its members, including enhanced security, improved checkpoint efficiency, and a better passenger experience. TSA currently has approximately 50 million Known Traveler Number holders and believes this number could double with industry support. TSA is requesting information on potential concepts, capabilities, and partnership models to grow the TSA PreCheck program through collaboration with airlines, other travel industry companies, and/or other interested parties. The travel industry has unique access to individuals as they are considering travel, making reservations, preparing for a trip, or engaging in other travel-related activities. These interactions may position travel industry entities to effectively promote TSA PreCheck and encourage eligible travelers to begin and complete enrollment. TSA is interested in receiving open-ended responses from industry regarding how partners could help increase TSA PreCheck enrollments. TSA does not intend to prescribe a single approach. Instead, TSA seeks information on a range of potential concepts that may include, but are not limited to, marketing, customer engagement, referral models, incentives, bundled offerings, online enrollment support, integration with existing travel platforms, enrollment event support, or other innovative concepts proposed by respondents. Industry partners may propose approaches that identify individuals who do not have a Known Traveler Number, engage customers during travel-related interactions, and encourage or support the TSA PreCheck enrollment process. Depending on the proposed approach, industry partners may collect limited information from interested individuals, such as name, date of birth, and preferred contact information, including email address and/or phone number. Industry partners may also propose other data collection, referral, voucher, payment, or enrollment support concepts for TSA�s consideration. Individuals enrolling in TSA PreCheck would still be required to complete an in-person enrollment through one of TSA�s three authorized enrollment providers, CLEAR, IDEMIA, or Telos. TSA is interested in learning more about capabilities that would allow industry partners, including airlines and travel industry companies, to market, promote, facilitate, refer, incentivize, or otherwise support TSA PreCheck enrollments. TSA is also interested in understanding how industry partners would measure results, report activity, support reconciliation, and structure compensation for efforts that result in increased TSA PreCheck enrollments. Industry partners may receive payment for activities that successfully support TSA PreCheck enrollment growth, subject to any future agreement and applicable requirements. TSA is seeking industry input on potential pricing structures, including, but not limited to, per-enrollment payments for completed enrollments, fixed-fee arrangements, milestone-based pricing, or other pricing concepts proposed by respondents. RESPONSES TO THIS RFI This section identifies the key information TSA requests from respondents. The topics below are intended to minimize respondent effort and help structure responses for ease of Government review. Respondents should also address the following topics, as applicable. Respondents are encouraged to propose their own concepts and are not limited to the examples provided. Response Element Description of Requested Information Illustrative Examples 1. Marketing Concepts Describe the concepts or capabilities the respondent believes could grow the TSA PreCheck population. Responses should explain how the proposed approach would reach, inform, encourage, or support travelers who may be interested in enrolling in TSA PreCheck Examples may include general TSA PreCheck marketing, targeted marketing, customer engagement during booking or trip preparation, referral programs, TSA PreCheck-specific benefits or bundles, loyalty program concepts, enrollment incentives, digital engagement strategies, temporary enrollment event support, or other innovative concepts. 2. Proposed Solution Description Describe the proposed solution or solutions to identify, engage, refer, capture, or otherwise support travelers interested in enrolling in TSA PreCheck. Respondents should explain the proposed customer journey and how the approach would support enrollment from initial engagement through completion, as applicable. For example, a respondent could propose a referral model in which a traveler is directed to an authorized enrollment provider and the partner receives payment if the traveler completes enrollment. A respondent could also propose capturing payment at the time of booking and providing the potential applicant with a voucher code that could be redeemed for enrollment. 3. Data Collection, Referral, and Transmission Approach Describe any proposed data collection, customer engagement, referral, payment, voucher, and transmission processes based on The respondent�s recommended technical and business approach. TSA has not yet finalized the minimum biographic data elements that industry partners may be required to collect and submit under any future approach. Depending on the proposed solution, TSA anticipates that this information may include name, date of birth, and preferred contact information. Respondents may also propose approaches that involve additional biographic information, payment information, referral information, voucher codes, or other data elements, as appropriate. Examples may include collecting limited biographic data, collecting additional biographic data such as passport number, address, or citizenship/permanent resident status, capturing payment information, issuing voucher codes, transmitting referral information, integrating with TSA�s authorized enrollment providers, or using another method to support the enrollment process. 4. Collaboration with Other Entities Identify whether the respondent intends to collaborate with other entities in support of the proposed concept. If so, describe the anticipated role of each entity. Examples may include collaboration with TSA�s current authorized enrollment providers, airlines, airports, travel agencies, online booking platforms, loyalty program providers, credit card issuers, or other travel industry companies. 5. Enrollment Completion Strategies and Incentives Describe any strategies the respondent may use to encourage travelers to complete the TSA PreCheck enrollment process after expressing interest or beginning an application. If applicable, describe any additional benefits the respondent may offer to encourage TSA PreCheck enrollment. Examples may include follow-up reminders, targeted communications, discounts, loyalty benefits, bundled travel benefits, targeted promotions, temporary enrollment event support, or other incentives. 6. Enrollment Impact Provide estimates of the number of individuals who may enroll in TSA PreCheck as a result of the proposed partnership. Respondents should include any assumptions used to develop those estimates. Examples of supporting assumptions may include estimated audience size, number of travelers without a Known Traveler Number, expected engagement rate, referral rate, application initiation rate, enrollment completion rate, campaign duration, or expected enrollment volume by channel. 7. Pricing Model and Assumptions Provide proposed pricing information for the respondent�s industry partnership

title: 6505--Request for Information (RFI) - Specialty Pharmacy – Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor (PPV) 2028
description: Department of Veterans Affairs, OALC, EPO AS7 Request for Information (RFI) Specialty Pharmacy Pharmaceutical Prime Vendor (PPV) 2028 Limited Distribution/Closed Distribution Products (CDP) are specialty medications that are generally high-cost, low-volume items for which manufacturers restrict distribution to a small, select network of authorized distributors outside traditional wholesale channels. Specialty Pharmacy dispensed prescriptions, must have a clinical justification or regulatory requirement to restrict dispensing to specialty pharmacies. These products may require additional pharmacy-performed activities such as product-specific registration, safety checks, monitoring, or compliance with manufacturer-mandated dispensing requirements. CDPs may or may not require pass-through delivery depending on the manufacturer's distribution model. The contractor shall ensure that all Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) items requiring specialty distribution including all those not currently/historically included or physically distributed through the Prime Vendor (PPV) are orderable by authorized ordering officers through the pharmaceutical prime vendor ordering platform. When a product requires specialty distribution, the pharmaceutical distributor shall coordinate fulfillment directly with the manufacturer-designated specialty distributor, even in cases where physical possession or shipment bypasses the pharmaceutical prime vendor. The goal is to provide seamless ordering access, accurate invoicing, and visibility into CDP transactions while maintaining compliance with manufacturer restrictions and ensuring timely, compliant delivery to VA facilities. Market Research Questions: Could this be included in the PPV scope? What is the potential impact on pricing, performance, and competition of bringing all FSS CDPs under PPV? Would it be reasonable for any one entity to coordinate the ordering and delivery for all LDD/CDP products that are on and may be added to FSS? Is this scope currently handled within your company? If not, how would your company intend to meet this requirement OR is there another avenue you would recommend? For all currently FSS-listed LDD/CDP products, can your company provide ordering access through the PPV (or a PPV-like) platform, regardless of distribution restrictions? Are there any FSS-listed CDPs your company historically has not been able to access due to manufacturer restrictions? If yes, please specify the nature of the barrier. When new CDP items are added to FSS, what onboarding timeline should VA expect for those items to become orderable through your system? Do any manufacturer agreements for FSS items explicitly prevent PPV(or PPV-like) -facilitated ordering? If so, what workarounds exist? What system changes are required to ensure all FSS CDPs whether physically stocked or drop-shipped are visible and orderable in the PPV (or PPV-like) ordering environment? What level of order visibility can be provided through your Ordering System tools for FSS CDPs fulfilled outside PPV (e.g., order acceptance, shipment status, delivery confirmation)? How would you provide VA with consistent reporting for all FSS CDP transactions, including reconciliation between the invoice and specialty distributor fulfillment? For FSS products subject to mandatory manufacturer programs, how does your company ensure compliance while still enabling ordering through PPV? What percentage of FSS-listed CDPs does your company currently distribute or coordinate? What system or operational investments would be required to scale your processes to support all FSS CDPs efficiently? Does your company recommend a single PPV (or PPV-like)-based mechanism for all FSS CDPs? Submission Instructions: Provide responses no later than 11AM Central November 16, 2026 Send responses via email to Karen.Ade@va.gov Telephone or fax responses will not be accepted. Include the following in your submission: Company Name Point of contact name, phone and email UEI and CAGE Code Socioeconomic designation(s), if applicable Important Notes: This announcement is not a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award. No contract will be awarded from this notice. Participation in this RFI (or lack thereof) does not preclude any vendor from submitting a proposal to the future PPV 2028 solicitation. All responses will be used for market research purposes only. The VA may contact respondents for clarification of submitted responses. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with responding to this notice or participating in any related activities. The VA appreciates industry's time and expertise in supporting the development of an effective PPV 2028 program, which supports delivery of pharmaceutical products to VA medical centers nationwide.

title: 3.45 GHz Engineering Support for Enduring Coordination (3-ESEC) Notice of Intent to Sole Source
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Defense Information Systems Agency/Defense Information Technology Contracting Organization intends to negotiate a sole source contract with Peraton, Inc. A sole source Justification & Approval document is being coordinated and, upon approval, a copy of it will be posted here on SAM.gov to comply with the public display requirements of FAR 6.301. The proposed contract action will continue providing support to facilitate the completion of the 3.45 GHz Engineering Support for Enduring Coordination (3-ESEC) for the 3450 � 3550 MHz band effort. BACKGROUND: In 2020, the White House and Department of Defense (DoD) established the America�s Mid-Band Initiative Team (AMBIT) to make 100 MHz of contiguous mid-band spectrum available for commercial 5G. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) subsequently authorized flexible-use licenses in the 3450�3550 MHz band (3.45 GHz band) and conducted Auction 110 in October 2021, offering 4,060 licenses nationwide. The band includes Cooperative Planning Areas (CPAs), which require coordination with DoD systems, and Periodic Use Areas (PUAs), where commercial access may be restricted during DoD operations. To support spectrum sharing, Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Command, Control, Communications, and Engineering (C3E) developed the 3.45 GHz Transition Plan, including an interim coordination portal and a future dynamic coordination system. In January 2022, Peraton was awarded the AMBIT Engineering Support for Initial Coordination (AESIC) task order to provide engineering analysis and manage coordination requests between DoD and commercial licensees. In April 2025, a follow-on 3.45 GHz Engineering Support for Enduring Coordination (3-ESEC) task order was awarded to Peraton and ends in May 2027. Since formal coordination began in October 2022, the AESIC/ESEC team has processed 3,192 coordination requests, 573,877 sectors, and delivered 2,080 results letters from commercial licensees. Because DoD systems will continue operating in the band, ongoing engineering support is needed to coordinate spectrum use between Military Departments and commercial licensees in CPAs and PUAs nationwide. Since October 2022, Peraton has supported more than 200 coordination meetings with commercial licensees and DoD stakeholders, building trusted relationships and a deep understanding of stakeholder priorities, operational requirements, and evolving mission needs. Primary objectives include: Manage and oversee 3.45 GHz coordination among Military Departments (MILDEPs), DoD CIO, PAE C3E, and commercial licensees to support Transition Plan execution and information sharing. Deliver consistent engineering, technical analysis, and subject-matter expertise to maximize spectrum sharing, minimize interference, and protect DoD spectrum-dependent systems. Develop, validate, deploy, and refine new Automated Spectrum Coordination System (ASCS) features and associated workflows, tools, algorithms, and business processes for dynamic spectrum coordination and interference deconfliction. Assess emerging technologies and commercial network proposals to identify potential impacts on DoD access and operations in the 3.45�3.55 GHz band. Provide data management and decision-support services to improve coordination data, inform government decision makers, and sustain DoD�s current and future radio frequency spectrum requirements. At this time, the incumbent contractor Peraton is the only known source capable of providing the required 3.45 GHz spectrum coordination engineering, analysis, and program-support services without unacceptable disruption to mission execution and within the remaining Spectrum Relocation Fund (SRF) Transition Plan period, which expires in December 2027. Peraton has provided continuous support for the 3.45 GHz coordination mission since 2022, giving it direct, mission-specific experience with the technical, operational, and stakeholder requirements of the effort. This proposed seven-month contract, including a potential 12-month option period, will provide continuity of support between the current contract�s expiration and completion of the SRF-funded requirement. Peraton�s continued performance is necessary to prevent a gap in support for ongoing coordination activities between the MILDEPs, DoD Chief Information Officer (CIO), PAE C3E, and commercial licensees. Peraton is uniquely positioned to continue performance because its incumbent workforce possesses established operational knowledge, specialized engineering expertise, mature coordination processes, and trusted stakeholder relationships developed through direct support of the 3.45 GHz spectrum-sharing mission since 2022. A transition to a new contractor would require substantial time and resources to transfer technical knowledge, establish access to relevant data and workflows, train personnel, validate engineering processes, and rebuild working relationships among Government and commercial stakeholders. These activities would create duplicative costs, require a significant ramp-up period, and introduce risk to the timeliness and consistency of spectrum-coordination support. The requirement involves a highly specialized spectrum-sharing environment requiring expertise in electromagnetic compatibility analysis, spectrum coordination, interference assessment, Automated Spectrum Coordination System (ASCS) workflows, and associated business-process development. Effective performance also depends on established communication and coordination among diverse stakeholders with competing operational and commercial interests. Through its support since 2022, Peraton has developed an extensive understanding of the 3.45 GHz coordination environment and the ability to rapidly modify business processes, technical analyses, and coordination approaches in response to changing stakeholder mission requirements and commercial network deployments. Given the limited remaining period of performance�seven months with a potential 12-month option�the Government does not anticipate that another source could reasonably absorb the transition costs and ramp-up time required to provide equivalent support within the available SRF funding window. Award to another source would increase cost, schedule, and mission risk without a commensurate benefit to the Government. Accordingly, continued award to Peraton Inc. is necessary to ensure uninterrupted 3.45 GHz coordination support, preserve continuity of operations, minimize avoidable transition costs, and enable completion of the SRF-funded requirement before funding expires in December 2027. The statutory authority for other than full and open competition is 10 USC 2304 (c) (1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Companies who believe they can provide this service must indicate their interest in writing within 15 days of this notification and include a detailed capability statement. No reimbursement for any cost connected with providing capability information will be provided. All responsible sources will be considered in evaluating the determination to issue a sole-source contract. Quotations or proposals received in response to this notice cannot be accepted since this synopsis cannot be considered a request for quote or a request for proposal. A solicitation will NOT be posted to SAM.gov due to the sole source nature of the requirement. The North American Classification System (NAICS) code 541511, Custom Computer Programming Services, will be used for determining company size status. The estimated dollar value of this contract is $3.7M. title: R402--Real Estate Acquisition Support Services (REASS) Recompete
description: Notice of VISN-Based Solicitation Structure Since release of the prior draft solicitation, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has refined the acquisition strategy for Real Estate Acquisition Support Services to align with the Veterans Health Administration s (VHA) evolving regional operating model. This revised approach supports VA s broader Restructure for Impact and Sustainability Effort (RISE), an organizational transformation directed by Executive Order 14210. RISE is intended to streamline VHA structures and processes, strengthen regional implementation and accountability, and support more consistent, coordinated, and responsive services for Veterans. Accordingly, VA has transitioned from a single nationwide contractor-pool approach to a multiple-award IDIQ structure organized by Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) Coverage Area. Benefits of the VISN-based approach include: Allowing qualified SDVOSB offerors to compete for one or more VISN Coverage Areas rather than requiring a nationwide proposal; Enabling offerors to focus proposals on geographic areas where they can demonstrate staffing, local-market resources, capacity, and lawful authority to operate; Supporting focused competition and VISN-specific commission pricing; Improving alignment between broker support, VA regional lease-acquisition operations, and local-market requirements; Strengthening accountability for contractor capacity, performance, quality control, and continuity of services within each VISN Coverage Area; and Supporting VA s broader effort to simplify operations, improve consistency, and enable more effective implementation at the regional and local levels. VA considered feedback received during the draft-solicitation/RFI phase. However, because the solicitation has been materially revised since the draft-solicitation/RFI phase, VA is not posting the historical draft-stage questions and Government responses. Those historical responses may not reflect the requirements, proposal instructions, evaluation approach, or procedures in the final solicitation. The final solicitation, its attachments, and any written amendments issued by the Contracting Officer are the only authoritative sources for solicitation requirements. Offerors shall submit questions concerning the final solicitation in accordance with the solicitation s instructions.

title: Request for Information (RFI) � Combat Rubber Raiding Craft (CRRC) Outboard Motors
description: This Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS)/Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational purposes and market research only; it does not constitute a solicitation. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for any expenses associated with preparing/submitting information in response to this posting. The information provided may be used by the Government in developing its acquisition strategy, statement of work/statement of objectives, and/or performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within their response as instructed later in this posting. The United States (US) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance & Special Operations Forces (ISR & SOF) Directorate, Special Warfare (SW) Program Office (AFLCMC/WISN) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing a CRRC Outboard Motor (OE). The current Guardian Angel (GA) weapon system relies on CRRC Outboard Motors that are nearing the end of their service life and no longer fully meet the evolving requirements of the Personnel Recover (PR) mission. The obsolescence of the current motor fleet restricts operational capabilities and increases mission risk. Specifically, the inability to operate reliably in rough seas limits the ability to conduct PR missions in certain geographic locations and weather conditions. The current program lacks a viable replacement solution that addresses these deficiencies, restores the weapon system�s full operational capability, and provides GA personnel with a reliable and effective CRRC-system for all operational environments. Furthermore, the decreased horsepower and increased unit weight of modern potential replacement EPA compliant 4-stroke Outboard Motors (OE) reduce operational capability and aerial delivery mission flexibility. description: Horse Racing Ireland (HRI) was established by the Irish Government under the Horse and Greyhound Racing Act 2001 and the Irish Horseracing Industry Act 1994. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to use this framework for any other business venture or industry body in which it is involved. The Irish Horseracing Regulatory Board(IHRB), while not an associate of HRI, may avail of this framework. Horse Racing Ireland (HRI) is seeking to purchase new Starting Stalls from suitably qualified suppliers for use at numerous racecourses over the Flat Racing Calendar. This framework maybe used for the supply of Starting Stalls for Horse Racing Ireland and its affiliates / associates, for up to 20 racecourses in the Republic of Ireland. It is envisaged that the initial requirement will be 2no 16 bay starting stall for Tipperary Racecourse. While there is no immediate further requirement, the framework will remain open for any further requirements that may appear over the 4 year duration

title: Land Mobile Radio Infrastructure Maintenance and Support
description: Description Notice of Intent to Sole Source 1. Procurement Office Background The Mission and Installation Contracting Command - Yuma Proving Ground (MICC-YPG), on behalf of the U.S. Army Yuma Proving Ground (USAYPG), Yuma, Arizona, is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of meeting the requirement described herein. This notice is issued to attempt to bolster government and industry coordination and partnership, as well as to determine if any other qualified commercial entities possess the capabilities to fulfill this requirement. 2. Scope of Requirement & Sole Source Intent The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract on a sole-source basis to Motorola Solutions, Inc. (809 Pinnacle Dr Ste G, Linthicum Heights, MD, 21090-2535). USAYPG currently operates an aging, proprietary Motorola Land Mobile Radio (LMR) network system (P25 digital system) manufactured by Motorola Solutions, Inc. This requirement is for the procurement of infrastructure maintenance and support subscription services, which include: Advanced Services & Cyber Support: 24/7/365 remote technical support provided via Motorola�s secure Operations Center. Diagnostics & Restorations: Real-time network management tools and OEM-level diagnostics capable of identifying, resolving, and restoring operations during critical system failures. Advanced Repair & Return (ARR): Quick-turnaround hardware repair and return services for proprietary LMR parts and components. On-line Technical Support: Tier-3/4 technical escalations beyond the capabilities of YPG organic personnel. Due to the proprietary nature of the P25 digital system and the significant Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) resources required for configuration management and information assurance, the government has determined that only Motorola Solutions, Inc. can provide these required sustainment services. This ensures that the network configuration remains in full compliance with Information Assurance requirements in accordance with Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 8500. 3. Information Sought (Capability Statement) If your firm possesses the capability to meet or exceed these requirements, the Government requests that you submit a Capability Statement demonstrating your technical and operational capacity. Please address the following inquiries in your response: OEM Support & Technical Capability: Describe your company's technical capability to provide 24/7 remote support, complex diagnostics, and physical parts repair/return for an aging proprietary Motorola P25 LMR network system. OEM Partnership & Authorization: Identify whether your firm is an authorized service provider or partner of Motorola Solutions, Inc., and clarify if your firm has the necessary agreements to utilize proprietary OEM diagnostics, software patches, and configuration tools. Information Assurance (DoDI 8500): Detail your technical approach to ensuring the LMR system remains in full compliance with DoD Information Assurance requirements under DoDI 8500. Commerciality: Does your company believe this infrastructure maintenance and support subscription service is a commercial item/service under FAR Part 12? NAICS Suitability: Do you agree that NAICS code 811210 (Communication Equipment Repair and Maintenance Services) is the most appropriate classification for this acquisition? If not, please propose an alternative NAICS code with justification. Socioeconomic Status & Business Size: Identify your business size standard under NAICS 811210 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, Women-Owned Small Business, or Large Business). Acquisition Approach: Identify whether your firm is interested in competing for this requirement as a Prime Contractor, or if you would pursue a subcontracting, joint-venture, or teaming arrangement. THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Request for Quotes (RFQ), or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. The Government is not seeking proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding will be solely at the interested party�s expense. The Government is interested in input from the small business community across all socioeconomic categories (including 8(a), Small Disadvantaged Business, HUBZone, SDVOSB, and WOSB) to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement at a fair market price. Any information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. NAICS Details Proposed services are classified under NAICS code 811210 - Communication Equipment Repair and Maintenance Services with the Corresponding index entry Communication Equipment Repair and Maintenance Services (Size Standard: $34.0M). This industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in repairing and maintaining communications equipment without retailing new communications equipment, such as commercial two-way radios, cellular/mobile phones, and carrier-line transmission equipment.
